title: Senator Bill Cassidy highlights HALT Fentanyl Act signing and anti-abortion advocacy
text:
Senator Bill Cassidy | Sen. Bill Cassidy Official Website
Senator Bill Cassidy | Sen. Bill Cassidy Official Website
U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D., has used his social media platform to highlight legislative and advocacy efforts on key issues including fentanyl regulation and anti-abortion policies.
On July 15, 2025, Cassidy announced an upcoming event at the White House, stating: "TOMORROW: I'm heading to the White House to join President Trump as he signs my HALT Fentanyl Act into law. I want fentanyl-free schools, homes, and businesses. So does President Trump. I’m proud we got this done for the American people."
The following day, July 16, 2025, Cassidy reported a meeting with Tara from Louisiana Right to Life. He wrote: "Met with my friend Tara from @LARighttoLife yesterday to talk about how we can continue to advance policies that protect the unborn. In Louisiana, we believe that every child has a right to life. I’ll always advocate to defend life here in Washington."
Later on July 16, Cassidy reiterated his participation in the White House event regarding fentanyl legislation: "Going to the White House today to join President Trump as he signs my HALT Fentanyl Act into law! The fentanyl crisis is driving overdose deaths across our nation. Proud to join the President in taking this step to protect our communities."
Senator Cassidy's HALT Fentanyl Act aims to address the ongoing opioid epidemic by increasing regulation of synthetic opioids such as fentanyl and enhancing penalties for trafficking offenses. The act is part of broader federal efforts in recent years to curb overdose deaths linked to synthetic opioids.
In addition to his work on drug policy, Cassidy has maintained active engagement with anti-abortion advocacy groups like Louisiana Right to Life. His public statements emphasize his commitment both at home in Louisiana and federally in Washington D.C., reflecting longstanding debates over abortion rights in U.S. politics.
